reviews.text: Very fun game, if you like Battle Brothers or War Tales you will enjoy this, especially for the price! I wish the map was randomly generated like Battle Brothers, also some of the random encounters are unwinnable. When my small party of 3 or 4 is attacked by an army of ogres in the first 12 days outside of one of the starter cities... it really hurts the enjoyment of the game. The worst part is that the game does not need random encounters at all when there are wandering armies on the game map. Please tune down random encounters, or just balance to what is possible based on your parties battle value, at least for the first in game month or so. In three hours I've lost multiple parties to random encounters before I just started save scumming every fight that was unwinnable.

Going off what I've seen so far and what's listed on the roadmap, this looks to be a higher fantasy alternative to Battle Brothers, but it lacks very much tactical depth. There is no terrain, elevation, or line of sight to deal with, only the occasional 1 hex decoration to attempt to use as a chokepoint. The action economy is heavily skewed in the enemies' favor due to having 6 guys to their potentially 20. More tactical features could be added later in development, and I assume the addition of fantasy classes will liven up the gameplay once your mage starts slinging fireballs and your cleric starts buffing the party. Until then, this is a game that I think is worth supporting and seeing how it comes out, but isn't quite worth recommending YET. I'm hopeful I can come back and change this to a Recommend in the future :)

This game is not too impressive. While I did not expect AAA type gameplay, the game itself is lacking. There is no story, there is limited character customization, battles feel very repetitive, random encounters are often enough to wipe out your entire party, etc. It appears that you can help villages become more prosperous when you complete quests, but they share none of the prosperity with you. Overall, I cannot recommend this game.

I gave this game an honest shake. This felt a lot like a worse version of titles like Wartales and Battle Brothers. This game tries to do a few things but does none of them well. The Good: I liked the pixel art aesthetic a lot. Sometimes fights would look insurmountable but usage of stun abilities or pin abilities helped secure victory - combat is more interesting when your abilities matter, but this is the minority of encounters in this game. The Awful: I found that the crafting elements that exist in this game are somewhat meaningless. You can tear apart basic level equipment and then use it to have blacksmiths in town forge new equipment. However, the weapons and equipment you can craft are extremely limited and there's no meaningful difference between weapons. Encounters are very random, there's not really a way to determine how intense the encounter is before you choose to fight it. The encounter descriptions are voiced with something that sounds like a text to speech program, and don't seem to say anything meaningful about encounters. The descriptions themselves are generalized enough that I would not be surprised to learn if they weren't AI generated. SOME player knowledge can help you know which encounters to skip, but I found it boiled down to seeing how many of what type of unit there were, and loading an autosave if they couldn't be beat. Characters you make/hire, just like the equipment, have no personality and feel indistinct from each other. Quests boil down to going to a specific location, clearing out a group of monsters, or clearing out a group of monsters in a fort (several monster fights in sequence). There are no meaningful drops from encounters, occasionally you can get an equipment slot upgrade, but most are just things worth static levels of currency. Locations are not distinct aside from art on the map and which services they offer. Quests are not unique. There's no overarching goal to the game. Grab some quests, make some cash, invest in some new equipment, maybe level up, rinse and repeat. There's party morale and social stats in the game but these effectively do nothing. You're either taking fights you can win, and winning, or you aren't. Some suggestions to improve: Develop some genuine sense of place and culture between areas. Have characters that are real and meaningful. I feel like this was attempted with character creation given that characters can have backgrounds, but static stat blocks are not enough. Have overarching conflict in the world that your mercenary band can engage with or try to profit from. Make exploration rewarding... Independent locations to explore, unique encounters, interesting loot to find, either more robust crafting or remove crafting entirely. Expand weapon and armor options and make them matter. Maybe give characters the ability to swap weapons to get an advantage on types of opponents? I LOVE the concept of leading a rag-tag band of mercs and forming them into a force to be reckoned with, but this game just doesn't have any heart or soul. Elements in the game don't have a sense of intent, it feels like they're in there because they're present in some other games, and none are developed well.

[h1]Early Access Game in an Early Stage of Development[h1] One needs the time and patience to deal a a lack of polish. The basic premise of the game is forming a band of adventurers to accept and perform quests for settlements in a territory. Completion of a quest results in loot in the form of dropped items, experience and pay from the source of the quest. These are used to level up individual members of the band, purchase or craft equipment, and recruit new members for the band. At present, there does not seem to be a final goal for a player to reach. Combat is somewhat basic. Looting after combat seems to be an all-or-nothing thing. Inventory management is very basic. I have found no way to get an item out of the party's shared inventory except by selling it or using it to craft equipment in one of the settlements. I am retired so I have the time to spend, others may not.
Game in a nutshell - A poor mans Battle Brothers.

A game that doesn't wow you at first, but slowly creeps up on your sense of enjoyment the longer you play. It's reminiscent of the SSI gold box games - Pool of Radiance, that sort of thing ( for those ancient and still living gamers who remember those days). Unfortunately, a lot of features aren't fully explained, so you wind up not knowing they're available until you stumble across them - and once you do, you wonder how you overlooked them. The "in game" narrator is surprisingly good ( making it feel a bit like a gaming session with a DM ) and you will often find yourself listening to the entire description of a room or fortress when you enter it. Surviving can be fairly difficult at the very beginning when you have poor and incomplete equipment - especially if you don't get a good selection of mercenaries to hire at the first town. Most of the low level missions are fair, but I did get a few that were impossible and the party had to run for their lives. Didn't come across any game breaking bugs. Overall, a fun time and well worth the price. The developer is active in the forums and open to player input,

Promising game in the making. Regular updates. Active and responsive devs. It's a good look and start. The gameplay is over world map into tactical battle. Mercenary group very D&D adjacent. Action, Bonus Action, and Movement. If you're familiar with 5e you'll feel the inspiration. Energy system in place that paces your abilities think mana bar that fills up every turn your vitality effects the regen rate. Recent update has given enemies abilities. I didn't actually play this game before enemies had abilities but they definitely make for challenging fights. You can get in over head very easy. Save often. You can and will run into bad fights that could lead to wipes. The balancing needs adjusting, but that will always be a push and pull. You travel the map, hit up towns, your mercs have personalities and preferences that shape how you'll be adventuring. Maybe your resting in towns more often. Maybe you're camping to rest. It's up to you. Looking forward to playing and testing the game more!

I want to clarify that this is a recommendation based off the 3 hours I've played so far on a $12 game. It is far from perfect, and by no means revolutionary in any way. This is not a sterling endorsement, in fact I'm going to highlight my issues with the game mostly. However, if you have a dozen dollars you don't want and enjoy the "tactical RPG" genre, you will not find this game offensive by any means. First of all, the name is horrible. It's still in early access, so I hope it's just a placeholder. Secondly, at this time, the tactics are pretty barebones. If you've played anything like this before, you'll learn the winning strategy pretty much immediately, and just continually employ it fight after fight. There are plenty of various enemy types, which is great, but running and gunning handles them all pretty much exactly the same. I like the overworld exploration, and the party progression as a whole. However, I find myself when the game gets monotonous, asking myself why I'm not just playing Wartales instead. It's not even that Wartales necessarily does the whole explore/craft/contract thing that much better, rather the Adventurers doesn't do much different, and what IS different makes progression a bit of a slog. I'm speaking entirely about the smithing mechanics, where breaking down items into resources takes in-game hours/days and money, and then smithing the item you actually wanted again takes in-game days and more money. Not to mention, you HAVE to return to the town you scrapped/crafted at, which makes sense but also keeps you locked down to an area for a while. Getting better stuff isn't worth the time to me. The narrator is a very nice touch, though I hope the AI is replaced by an actual voice actor like proposed. Nine times out of ten it sounds good, but then every now and then its awful garbage that takes me out. I'm not one to bash small dev teams for using AI during early access, but it's gotta be gone at full release. That and the gameplay simply has to be better. Overall, this game teeter on being a no, so you have to like these kinds of games to get much enjoyment out of it at this point. Maybe later after more updates, this will all be moot, but right now it's worth exactly 12 dollars, preferably less.
